source.title: Generalization Bound of Gradient Flow through Training Trajectory and Data-dependent Kernel
source.authors: Yilan Chen; Zhichao Wang; Wei Huang; Andi Han; Taiji Suzuki; Arya Mazumdar

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments relating a proposed training-trajectory bound to measured generalization gaps, including an experiment with label noise. These are conceptual tests of measured properties that track the gap, but do not test the claim versions' specified comparisons or interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures training/test loss and error and compares a trajectory-based bound Γ with the generalization gap. It reports that Γ captures the gap in experiments, including one with random-label noise. Optimizer, architecture, width and training details are not systematically varied to test V1–V6; sharpness and memorized-example removal are not tested. Figure-only results are described qualitatively in the text, so no numerical values are reconstructed. Results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether its trajectory-gradient bound Γ tracks generalization gaps, which is outside V1–V8. Label corruption alone does not establish V1's coexistence of near-perfect random-label fit and natural-label generalization; Γ is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive loss-path-kernel generalization bounds for gradient flow and stochastic gradient flow and report that the leading term Γ tracks measured gaps. The experiments use finite-step GD and SGD; the theory's practical extension to large learning rates remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The claim versions concern empirical comparisons of memorization, architecture, optimizers, batch size, explicit regularization, sharpness and memorized-example removal. This paper instead derives a gradient-flow bound and reports experiments comparing that bound with measured gaps; its SGD experiments use finite-step training.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the gap and Γ increase with the portion of label noise; in Appendix A, the MNIST two-layer network is described as showing less overfitting than the other experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Γ qualitatively tracks measured loss generalization gaps during training; additional appendix experiments report similar tracking, with less overfitting on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A training-trajectory gradient measure can qualitatively track loss generalization gaps in the reported neural-network experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The reported generalization gap and Γ increase with the proportion of corrupted labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption increases the loss generalization gap and trajectory-gradient bound in this binary CIFAR-10 experiment.

record.problems: The experiment results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The label-noise experiment does not report random-label training fit or held-out accuracy against chance. The authors state that their analysis focuses on gradient flow and that behavior of other algorithms remains unclear; their experiments also include finite-step GD and SGD.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside strong natural-label held-out accuracy using the same architecture and recipe, with random-label held-out accuracy at chance.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity or transferred initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The norm-bound comparison in Section 7 does not test V7's sharpness ranking. Appendix experiments add no result bearing on V1–V8. The supplied manuscript identifies itself as a preprint under review, so the record's NeurIPS peer-review designation is unsupported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label and random-label generalization accuracy for the specified architectures or report random-label fit and held-out accuracy.
No width sweep across the interpolation threshold or test-error comparison beyond zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No large-batch versus small-batch comparison testing a generalization penalty.
Γ is a trajectory-gradient bound, not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in this version; no comparison of sharpness measures or correlations among networks at similar training loss.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: two-layer NN of 400 hidden nodes and Softplus activation function
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, test loss, test error and Γ during full-batch gradient descent; compared Γ with the generalization gap.
rows.measure: Γ compared with true generalization gap
rows.value: Figure 2 shows Γ captures the generalization gap well; the gap first increases and then converges after sufficient training time.
rows.note: The text qualitatively describes the figure but does not give numerical gap or Γ values. This measures a proposed bound's relationship to the gap, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: This evaluates the study's own bound, not a claim version. The qualitative tracking result is stated explicitly, but it cannot determine any version's effect. The trajectory description primarily describes Γ.

rows.subject: ResNet 18
rows.operation_detail: Measured training loss, test loss, test error and Γ during SGD training; compared Γ with the true generalization gap.
rows.measure: Γ compared with true generalization gap
rows.value: Figure 1 shows Γ correlates well with the true generalization gap; text says the bound characterizes overfitting and feature unlearning after long-term training.
rows.note: No numerical values are stated in the text. The figure description does not report a result for any claim version.
rows.check: This evaluates the study's own bound. ResNet-18 training provides no architecture, optimizer, or batch-size comparison bearing on V3–V5.

rows.subject: two-layer NN
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization gap and Γ while training on data with corrupted labels; examined their change with label-noise portion.

conditions.value: labels corrupted with random labels; portion varied

rows.measure: Generalization gap and Γ as label-noise portion increases
rows.value: Text states that Γ captures the gap well and increases with the portion of label noise; the gap also increases.
rows.note: The experiment concerns random-label noise, but the supplied description does not state whether the network fits random labels or give held-out accuracy versus chance; it therefore does not test V1.
rows.check: Increasing loss gaps with label noise does not establish near-perfect random-label training accuracy or chance held-out accuracy. Neither quantity is readable from the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
